messages:
Anna: FYI customer reported duplicate provisional charges after a streaming retry that routed to another region. Console showed two provisional rows then the final confirmed line — confusing the customer. Need a short plan to reduce noise and make accounting deterministic.

Mike: can you share the raw session/request ids from the traces? want to see whether provisional rows are created per-route or per-session.

Anna: pasted logs from the request: 
```
{"session_id":"s-9f0a","request_id":"r-3421","route":"us-west-2","toolcall_id":"tc-77","provisional_tokens":312,"state":"provisional"}
{"session_id":"s-9f0a","request_id":"r-3421","route":"eu-central-1","toolcall_id":"tc-77","provisional_tokens":312,"state":"provisional"}
{"session_id":"s-9f0a","request_id":"r-3421","route":"eu-central-1","toolcall_id":"tc-77","confirmed_tokens":312,"state":"confirmed"}
```

Liam: yep, router is emitting a provisional ledger row on each attempted route. When the final route confirms we mark that one confirmed but earlier provisionals remain visible in console. That is accurate but noisy.

Jess: UX idea: collapse provisionals by (session_id + toolcall_id) in the console and show an aggregated provisional token count. Expand reveals per-route provisional breakdown and final reconciliation.

Sara: agree on fold-by-session, but important caveat: if token counts differ across routes (e.g., truncation or partials) we must surface per-route deltas when expanded. Don9t hide differences.

Mike: Architect question: should provisional rows be deduped in the ledger, or only hidden in console? Deduping ledger entries changes accounting semantics.

Liam: operationally safest is console-level folding first (no ledger change). But longer-term we should add a stable provisional identifier so retries carry the same provisional key and ledger can safely dedupe or stitch entries.

Jess: proposal for internal headers and API fields: add X-Session-Id, X-Toolcall-Id, X-Provisional-Id and optional truncation_reason (client_abort | server_truncation | upstream_eof). Example: 
```
POST /v1/streams
X-Session-Id: s-9f0a
X-Toolcall-Id: tc-77
X-Provisional-Id: prov-01a2b3
```
This lets the router forward the same provisional id when it retries across routes.

Anna: router must preserve provisional id and also tag whether provisional was generated by SDK or router fallback. Add provisional_origin: sdk | router to telemetry.

Izzy: logging team prefers an explicit provisional_origin tag so we can filter SDK-created vs router-generated provisional ids. That helps root-cause when older SDKs don't emit the header.

Mike: billing rule question: when a toolcall gets truncated by the callee (upstream_eof), who gets charged? Current implementation attributes token usage to the route that executed the toolcall. I think bill the customer (root request) and do a backend settlement/credit to the provider if internal. For external provider contracts we need explicit terms. Will add charge_owner on confirmed events.

Liam: agree. Ledger should record charge_owner and provenance. For cross-route retries we should show provisional entries but the final confirmed event determines charge_owner and final token count.

Jess: telemetry/metrics to add: billing.provisional.count_by_route, billing.provisional.stale_rate (provisionals without confirmed after threshold), billing.finalize_latency_ms, billing.truncation.count_by_reason. Suggest alert: billing.provisional.stale_rate > 0.03 for 15m.

Sara: add console UX changes: collapsed high-level row per request with status badge (pending / finalized), aggregated provisional tokens, expand to see each provisional by route + final confirmed. Include link to trace and request ids. Reuse existing expand pattern.

Mike: ownership: Billing (Mike) owns ledger design and reverse-credit flow; Eng-Platform (Liam, Anna) owns router + telemetry; DevEx (Jess) adds SDK headers; Product/Design (Sara) owns console UX. Ops-bot: scheduled canary window?

ops-bot: scheduled deploy: router canary 2026-03-22T16:00Z to 2026-03-22T18:00Z.

Anna: rollout plan sketch: 1) Console fold by session+toolcall_id (fast follow). 2) Add provisional headers in SDKs + router preservation. 3) Feature-flag ledger dedupe using provisional_id; canary 5% for 48h. 4) Full rollout and deprecation of noisy provisional rows in UI.

Jess: when SDKs don't emit provisional_id router will generate one; ensure router includes provisional_origin=router and copies id downstream.

Mike: i'll draft RFC describing ledger key change: use (session_id, provisional_id) as dedupe key, add charge_owner on confirmed events, and outline reverse-credit settlement for internal providers.

Sara: i'll mock the collapsed UI and post screenshots to #design. Keep fold default collapsed to avoid surprising users.

Anna: please add short bullets to RFC for constraints: dedupe key semantics, fallback behavior when provisional_id missing, alert thresholds, and expansion UX. I'll consolidate and schedule 30-min review tomorrow. High-priority for next sprint.

Liam: one more: add a small DB migration plan for ledger dedupe index; make sure we can backfill provisional_origin for recent provisional rows to avoid confusion in metrics.

Izzy: logging will add provisional_origin tag and a metric to surface router-generated provisional id counts.

Anna: great. thanks all. reconvene after RFC comments. :thumbsup:
